advances: This proves an exact reduction of the residual weighted-threshold inequality to one cross-direction contact-balance implication on the larger outer slice. It retains each direction's unique actual allocation, every zero-demand and capacity endpoint, and the complete maximizing set in the endpoint max-plus convolution. It does not assert or prove the remaining contact-balance implication.
author: mp_r234_residual_balance
proof:
Accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971` gives the fixed feasible allocation interval
\[
L=\max\{0,t-m\},\qquad U=\min\{t,a_1\},
\tag{9}
\]
and proves that \(p_\ell=a_*(q_\ell)\) lies in \([L,U]\). Hence
\[
0\le b_\ell=t-p_\ell\le t-L\le m.
\tag{10}
\]
This proves the first assertion about \(b_\ell\).

We next prove (3), including every endpoint convention. Fix \(\ell\), suppress \(q_\ell\), and use the notation of accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971`,
\[
A(a)=Q_{1,q_\ell}(a),\qquad
B(a)=\frac12\overline E_{q_\ell}(t-a),\qquad
\delta(a)=A(a)-B(a).
\]
There are exactly three optimizer regimes.

If the optimizer is \(L\) and \(\delta(L)\ge0\), then there are two subcases. If \(L=0\), the actual value formula gives
\[
\rho_\ell=B(0)\le A(0)=Q_{1,q_\ell}(0).
\]
The closed cap at or below this lower support endpoint has area zero, so
\[
F_{1,q_\ell}(\rho_\ell)=0=L=p_\ell.
\]
If \(L>0\), the actual value formula instead gives
\[
\rho_\ell=A(L)=Q_{1,q_\ell}(L),
\]
and strict invertibility of the cap function from accepted fact `17ca54faa05ad878` gives
\[
F_{1,q_\ell}(\rho_\ell)=L=p_\ell.
\]
The latter subcase includes the capacity-active endpoint demand \(b_\ell=m\).

If the optimizer is \(U\) and \(\delta(U)\le0\), there are again two subcases. If \(U=t\), including the actual zero endpoint demand \(b_\ell=0\), the value formula gives
\[
\rho_\ell=A(t)=Q_{1,q_\ell}(t),
\]
so \(F_{1,q_\ell}(\rho_\ell)=t=U=p_\ell\). If \(U<t\), then \(U=a_1\), and
\[
\rho_\ell=B(U)\ge A(U)=Q_{1,q_\ell}(a_1).
\]
Thus the closed middle cap is full and
\[
F_{1,q_\ell}(\rho_\ell)=a_1=U=p_\ell.
\]
This includes the middle-capacity endpoint.

Finally, in the crossing regime,
\[
\rho_\ell=A(p_\ell)=B(p_\ell)=Q_{1,q_\ell}(p_\ell),
\]
so strict invertibility again gives (3). Coincidences such as \(t=m\) or \(t=a_1\) are already contained in these displayed subcases. Throughout this argument, the actual value \(E_q(0)=-\infty\) is used in (1); the finite extension \(\overline E_q(0)\) is used only to classify the optimizer, exactly as in accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971`.

The continuity of the endpoint quantiles in accepted fact `17ca54faa05ad878` makes the maximand in (4) continuous on the compact interval \([0,b]\). Hence every \(\mathcal U_q(b)\) is nonempty and compact. For \(b>0\), accepted fact `17ca54faa05ad878` gives the exact full max-plus identity
\[
E_q(b)=
\max_{0\le u\le b}
\left(
Q_{j,q}(u)+Q_{k,q}(b-u)
\right).
\tag{11}
\]
At \(b=0\), accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971` gives the separate finite right-endpoint extension
\[
\overline E_q(0)=Q_{j,q}(0)+Q_{k,q}(0),
\tag{12}
\]
while the actual optimization convention remains \(E_q(0)=-\infty\). Thus (4) retains the complete endpoint infimal convolution without changing (1).

Assume now that \(W>0\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^2\), at least one index \(\ell\) satisfies
\[
q_\ell\cdot x<\rho_\ell.
\tag{13}
\]
Indeed, if all reverse weak inequalities held, then
\[
0=\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell q_\ell\right)\cdot x
\ge\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell\rho_\ell=W>0,
\]
a contradiction. Hence the three closed middle caps
\[
A_1\cap\{x:q_\ell\cdot x\le\rho_\ell\}
\]
cover \(A_1\). Their areas are \(p_\ell\) by (3). Finite subadditivity proves (5).

For arbitrary choices \(u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\), one has \(0\le u_\ell\le b_\ell\). Therefore (2) and (5) give
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3u_\ell
\le\sum_{\ell=1}^3b_\ell
=3t-\sum_{\ell=1}^3p_\ell
\le3t-a_1.
\tag{14}
\]
It remains to prove the strict inequality in (6). Write, as in accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`,
\[
r=\frac mM,\qquad s=\frac{a_1}{M}.
\]
Since
\[
\frac{3t-a_1}{M}
=\frac{2+2r-s}{3},
\tag{15}
\]
the inequality \(3t-a_1<M\) is equivalent to
\[
s>2r-1.
\tag{16}
\]
If \(0<r\le1/2\), then \(2r-1\le0<s\). If \(r>1/2\), the residual lower bound in accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e` is
\[
s>\frac{3r+2\sqrt r-1}{2},
\]
and
\[
\frac{3r+2\sqrt r-1}{2}-(2r-1)
=\frac{1-r+2\sqrt r}{2}>0.
\]
Thus (16) holds throughout the strict residual strip. Equations (14)-(16) prove (6).

Fix any choices \(u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\). Suppose, contrary to (7), that
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3
\alpha_\ell Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)\ge0.
\tag{17}
\]
The three closed halfplanes
\[
\{x:q_\ell\cdot x\le Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)\}
\tag{18}
\]
cover \(\mathbb R^2\). Otherwise some \(x\) would satisfy all three strict reverse inequalities, and positive weighting would give
\[
0=\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell q_\ell\right)\cdot x
>
\sum_{\ell=1}^3
\alpha_\ell Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)\ge0,
\]
a contradiction. By the endpoint normalization and strict cap inverses in accepted fact `17ca54faa05ad878`,
\[
\left|A_j\cap
\{x:q_\ell\cdot x\le Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)\}\right|
=u_\ell
\tag{19}
\]
for all \(0\le u_\ell\le a_j\), including the zero and full-cap endpoints. Intersecting the cover (18) with \(A_j\), taking areas, and using (19) yields
\[
M=a_j\le\sum_{\ell=1}^3u_\ell,
\]
contrary to (6). This proves the strict inequality (7) for every selection.

Each \(\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\) is compact, so their product is compact, and the weighted quantile sum is continuous on it. Its maximum is attained. Since every attained value is strictly negative by (7), the maximum is strictly negative, proving (8).

If (CB) were established, a triple with \(W>0\) would satisfy both (8) and the opposite weak inequality in (CB), which is impossible. Hence (CB) would imply \(W\le0\) for every positive-spanning triple. Accepted fact `9328166a552ec875` identifies these inequalities as the numerical cross-direction condition for the exact profile halfplanes, while accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` shows that a global failure produces precisely a positive-spanning three-profile certificate. Therefore (CB) would finish the registered residual bridge. No assertion that (CB) is already proved has been used.

It remains to verify the two required calibrations. In accepted fact `2fdbcddaa185b50e`, with \(D=1/2\),
\[
M=D(1+2\varepsilon^2)^2,\qquad
a_1=D,\qquad
T=D(2+5\varepsilon^2+4\varepsilon^4).
\]
Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
M-(3t-a_1)
&=D\left(1+4\varepsilon^2+4\varepsilon^4
-\frac13-\frac{10}{3}\varepsilon^2
-\frac83\varepsilon^4\right)\\
&=\frac12\left(
\frac23+\frac23\varepsilon^2+\frac43\varepsilon^4
\right)>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
\]
That accepted fact also verifies \(0<t<a_1+m\), so the exact allocation and endpoint formulas used above apply, and it gives a positive-spanning triple with \(W>1\). The proof of (3), (5), and (7) uses the residual strip only to obtain \(3t-a_1<M\); equation (20) supplies that inequality directly for this family. Hence its exact direction-dependent contact sets satisfy the strict negative signature (8). This proves that (CB) is false as an unconditional compatibility statement and that the large-slice counterexample is not bypassed by the reduction.

In accepted fact `74e60bee4b401289`,
\[
h_S((1,0))>\frac{2T}{9}=t.
\]
Accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` identifies the exact middle depth region with the profile intersection, so
\[
0=q\cdot0\ge\rho_q(t)
\qquad(q\in\mathbb S^1).
\]
Thus every positive-spanning triple in that example has \(W\le0\), and the antecedent of (CB) is false. Its rejected two-routing witness uses the support-extreme reflected caps at a prescribed point; those caps are not selected from (4) after fixing the unique actual \(p_\ell=a_*(q_\ell)\). Therefore the two-routing counterexample does not refute (CB), but it does rule out replacing the exact contact sets (4) by either reflected route or by a fixed allocation.
statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compatible nonempty compact convex bodies with nonempty interiors. Put
\[
a_i=|A_i|,\qquad T=a_0+a_1+a_2,\qquad
M=\max\{a_0,a_2\},\qquad m=\min\{a_0,a_2\},
\qquad t=\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
Assume the full strict residual strip of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Choose \(j\in\{0,2\}\) with \(a_j=M\), and put \(k=2-j\), so \(a_k=m\).

For \(q\in\mathbb S^1\), let
\[
F_{i,q}(c)=|A_i\cap\{x:q\cdot x\le c\}|
\]
and let \(Q_{i,q}:[0,a_i]\to\mathbb R\) be the endpoint-normalized cap quantile
\[
Q_{i,q}(0)=\min_{x\in A_i}q\cdot x,\qquad
Q_{i,q}(u)=\inf\{c:F_{i,q}(c)\ge u\}\quad(0<u\le a_i).
\]
Use the exact profile threshold \(\rho_q(t)\), the actual conventions
\[
D_{1,q}(0)=E_q(0)=-\infty,
\]
and the unique optimizer \(a_*(q)\) in
\[
\rho_q(t)=
\min_{0\le a\le t}
\max\left\{D_{1,q}(a),\frac12E_q(t-a)\right\}
\tag{1}
\]
from accepted facts `17ca54faa05ad878` and `65512ded3a06d971`.

Fix a noncollinear positive-spanning triple
\[
q_1,q_2,q_3\in\mathbb S^1,\qquad
\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3>0,\qquad
\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell q_\ell=0.
\]
Write
\[
\rho_\ell=\rho_{q_\ell}(t),\qquad
p_\ell=a_*(q_\ell),\qquad
b_\ell=t-p_\ell,\qquad
W=\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell\rho_\ell.
\tag{2}
\]
Then \(0\le b_\ell\le m\), and
\[
F_{1,q_\ell}(\rho_\ell)=p_\ell
\qquad(\ell=1,2,3).
\tag{3}
\]

For \(0\le b\le m\), define the full endpoint contact set
\[
\mathcal U_q(b)=
\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{0\le u\le b}
\left(
Q_{j,q}(u)+Q_{k,q}(b-u)
\right).
\tag{4}
\]
This is nonempty and compact. When \(b=0\), (4) is the singleton \(\{0\}\) and records only the finite endpoint extension
\[
Q_{j,q}(0)+Q_{k,q}(0);
\]
it does not replace the actual value \(E_q(0)=-\infty\) used in (1). Formula (4) includes \(b=m\), zero-mass splits, and full-cap splits.

If \(W>0\), then
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3p_\ell\ge a_1,
\tag{5}
\]
and, for every choice \(u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\),
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3u_\ell
\le 3t-a_1<M,
\tag{6}
\]
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3
\alpha_\ell Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)<0.
\tag{7}
\]
Equivalently, every violation of the desired weighted-threshold inequality has the strict larger-slice contact signature
\[
\max_{\substack{
u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\\
\ell=1,2,3}}
\sum_{\ell=1}^3
\alpha_\ell Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)<0.
\tag{8}
\]

Consequently, the following single implication would finish the residual weighted-threshold theorem:
\[
W>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\max_{\substack{
u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\\
\ell=1,2,3}}
\sum_{\ell=1}^3
\alpha_\ell Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)\ge0.
\tag{CB}
\]
More precisely, if (CB) is proved from compatibility and the full strict residual strip for every positive-spanning triple, then \(W\le0\) for every such triple. Accepted facts `9328166a552ec875` and `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` then identify this as the required bridge ruling out an empty exact middle depth region under a global counterexample.

The calibration is exact. The compatible large-slice family in accepted fact `2fdbcddaa185b50e` violates the unconditional weighted-threshold inequality and also has the strict negative contact signature (8), so (CB) cannot hold without the residual hypotheses. The residual two-routing example in accepted fact `74e60bee4b401289` does not violate (CB): its true depth point forces \(W\le0\), while its two reflected support-extreme routes are not the directionwise contact sets (4).
